provenance.citation: Hu D., Beauvais M. L., Kamm G. E., Mullens B. G., Sanchez Monserrate B. A., Vornholt S. M., Chupas P. J., Chapman K. W., J. Am. Chem. Soc. 145 (2023) 26545-26549
provenance.extraction: Colour classification of the raster Fig. 2 image by scripts/extract_chapman_fig2.py (D. Naumov, commit f135e65; data/digitized_inputs/chapman2023_fig2/extracted_phase_fractions.csv, no manual clicking), then scripts/chapman_to_dataset.py: each grid value is the mean of the 3 extracted 0.05 min columns within 0.051 min of the grid time, because the columns are pixel samples of one drawn curve and using all ~200 would overstate the information; columns before 0.3 min overlap the heating strip, axis line and Li2CO3 label, so the grid starts at 0.3 min and no column with t < 0.3 min is averaged into any value (the 0.3 min point is the mean of the 0.30 and 0.35 min columns only); the grid stops at 9.5 min for every temperature because the last columns of one panel are an edge artefact (details in the converter docstring, not repeated here so that no file carries another temperature's values); Ti fractions converted to formula units per mol Ti (Li4Ti5O12 divided by 5); no t = 0 point.
provenance.notes: Not yet verified. To do (meta.json): Spot-check 5-10 points per panel against the printed figure (for example Li2TiO3 at 0.5, 1, 2, 5 min and the time anatase reaches zero) and compare reconstruction.png with Fig. 2. Known bias: this panel's extracted Li2TiO3 band reaches 55.4 wt % (at 0.75 min, in the columns used here) against the about 52 wt % maximum stated by the authors, a bias of about 2 wt % most likely from the 1-2 px boundary lines; treat every phase fraction as carrying about 1-2 wt % systematic error. reconstruction.png in the input folder is our re-plot, not the published figure.

conditions.precursors: 5:2 TiO2 (anatase):Li2CO3 molar, pelletized, loaded in a capillary
conditions.notes: Sample moved into a pre-heated hot zone; heating takes under 10 s (the 'Heating' strip in the paper's Fig. 3, about the first 0.17 min), and t = 0 is insertion, so the sample is below temperature_C for roughly the first 0.17 min. Atmosphere not stated. c0 is the nominal mix (0.4 Li2CO3 per Ti from the 5:2 molar ratio). Li2CO3 is not a series: the authors state its peaks are no longer distinguishable after about 30 s, and the extraction shows only a ~1-2 wt % line-width strip to the end of the panel, so it appears only in c0.

series.reported_unit: weight % (normalised stack of Rietveld phase fractions)
series.conversion: mol per mol Ti = mean(tifrac_anatase) over 3 pixel columns (2 at 0.3 min); tifrac_anatase from wt % with M = 79.866 g/mol, 1 Ti per formula unit

series.reported_unit: weight % (normalised stack of Rietveld phase fractions)
series.conversion: mol per mol Ti = mean(tifrac_rutile) over 3 pixel columns (2 at 0.3 min); tifrac_rutile from wt % with M = 79.866 g/mol, 1 Ti per formula unit

series.reported_unit: weight % (normalised stack of Rietveld phase fractions)
series.conversion: mol per mol Ti = mean(tifrac_Li2TiO3) over 3 pixel columns (2 at 0.3 min); tifrac_Li2TiO3 from wt % with M = 109.75 g/mol, 1 Ti per formula unit

series.reported_unit: weight % (normalised stack of Rietveld phase fractions)
series.conversion: mol per mol Ti = mean(tifrac_Li4Ti5O12) over 3 pixel columns (2 at 0.3 min) / 5; tifrac_Li4Ti5O12 from wt % with M = 459.08 g/mol, 5 Ti per formula unit

quality.basis_note: Amounts are formula units per mole of total Ti. The figure plots weight % as a normalised stack (anatase, rutile, Li4Ti5O12, Li2TiO3, Li2CO3 summing to 100); the extraction converted wt % to the fraction of Ti in each Ti-bearing phase with nominal molar masses (TiO2 79.866, Li2TiO3 109.75, Li4Ti5O12 459.08 g/mol; 1, 1, 5 Ti per formula unit), and this converter divides the Li4Ti5O12 Ti fraction by 5. Because the stack is normalised, anatase + rutile + Li2TiO3 + 5 x Li4Ti5O12 = 1 at every point by construction, so a Ti closure check cannot reveal unobserved or amorphous Ti-bearing material. Nominal molar masses were used although the authors report Li-deficient Li2-xTiO3, so the Li2TiO3 amount is approximate. In this panel the Li2TiO3 Ti fraction peaks at 0.486 at 0.8 min on this grid (0.488 at 0.75 min in the 0.05 min columns), above the 0.40 that stoichiometric Li2TiO3 allows with 0.8 Li per Ti in the mix. With nominal stoichiometries (2 Li per Li2TiO3, 4 per Li4Ti5O12) the observed phases would hold 1.02 Li per Ti at 1.5 min and 0.95 at 9.5 min, against 0.8 supplied: either Li2TiO3 is strongly Li-deficient, the extracted Li2TiO3 band is too wide, or the plotted fractions do not balance Li; this dataset cannot tell which.
